<Note>
Current runtime policy: Docker setup and Docker-backed E2E/image CI are paused;
the Docker cron runner is retired. Rust and TanStack Start are not in use and
must not be run, tested, or updated until further notice. Retained Docker and
migration sections below are historical procedures. Current hosted Next.js,
package, Worker, database, and mobile workflows retain their own gates. See the
[active runtime map](/build/devops/active-runtime).
</Note>

This page explains how Tuturuuu moves from code to running environments.

## Generated Release Formatting

Release Please initially pushes generated manifests, then amends that commit
with Biome formatting before approval. Biome cancels superseded runs per Git ref
so the intermediate unformatted commit cannot keep running beside its replacement.
Inspect the run for the current release PR head when diagnosing a failure.
Cancelled or skipped runs do not publish PR reports. Generated release branches
use the release workflow's formatter rather than separate automatic formatting
PRs; their final commits still receive the normal format and lint checks.

After formatting, `scripts/ci/normalize-release-description.js` also consolidates
identical bullets in each component section of the generated PR description. It
preserves source references, distinct wording, component summaries, and review
bot content. This runs even when generated files need no formatting changes.

Before formatting, `scripts/ci/normalize-release-notes.js` combines repeated
descriptions within each new release section, retaining every distinct commit
and PR link. It excludes narrowly identified integration-only merge commits.
The existing production release heading marks the immutable published boundary;
if that boundary is missing, normalization fails instead of rewriting history.
The generated release commit is amended using the existing exact-SHA lease.
No package version, dependency resolution or published changelog is rewritten.

## Branch-to-Environment Map

| Branch or event                     | What deploys                                                                                       | Follow-up automation                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Feature branch push                 | CI only; Vercel preview deployments require trusted manual dispatch from `main` with `preview_ref` | None by default                                                                                                                      |
| `main` push                         | Platform Vercel preview build validation                                                           | `supabase-staging.yaml` independently applies staging migrations and records the exact main SHA                                                |
| `production` push                   | Platform Vercel production deployment                                                              | `supabase-production.yaml` can apply production migrations after the deployment and staging prerequisites pass                       |
| `main` push for `apps/discord`      | Discord Modal deployment after Python CI succeeds                                                  | None                                                                                                                                 |
| Manual `workflow_dispatch`          | Depends on workflow                                                                                | Bypasses normal branch trigger timing, but not the workflow logic; production Supabase migration dispatches must select `production` |
| Self-hosted server after `git pull` | Docker deploy from current checkout                                                                | Optional blue/green cutover through `bun serve:web:docker:bg`                                                                        |

## Hosted Web Release Flow

### Preview

- Preview workflows are named `vercel-preview-<app>.yaml`.
- Most preview workflows are manual-only from `main` with a required
  `preview_ref`; `vercel-preview-platform.yaml` also triggers on protected
  `main` pushes so the staging database workflow receives a same-SHA platform
  build signal.
- `e2e-tests.yaml` also runs only on non-`production` pushes; production
  promotion relies on the already-green validation before the branch is
  promoted plus the production build-validation gates below.
- Production workflows cancel superseded per-app runs only when a newer
  `production` push arrives; `main` commits and manual recovery runs leave an
  active production deployment untouched.
- Each deploy job is bound to a `vercel-preview-<app>` GitHub Environment and
  introduces Vercel credentials only after dependency installation.
- Platform preview is build validation only; on-premise machines own the actual
  `apps/web` runtime deployment.
- Satellite preview deploys remain the normal Vercel validation surface for
  branch work and merged `main` changes.
- Platform preview can reuse a successful same-SHA production platform build
  marker to avoid redundant preview builds. Production does not reuse preview
  markers because it must build and deploy the prebuilt production artifacts.

### Staging Database

- `supabase-staging.yaml` runs on protected `main` pushes independently of Vercel
  preview results. Main-only manual dispatch remains available for staging repair.
- Before checkout, its shell gate exactly binds runner/event refs, repository name
  and ID, and push `after` to `GITHUB_SHA`. Deleted pushes, unprotected push refs,
  unsupported events, case variants and non-full SHAs fail closed. The verified SHA
  must be identical to or behind fully qualified `refs/heads/main`.
- Supabase Production retains its named-upstream proof for planner and staging
  completions, including the new staging producer's `push` event. Other
  `workflow_run` consumers keep their existing canonical trigger proof.
- Expression `==` ignores case, so `head_branch == 'main'` also admits a branch
  named `Main`. Job `if` guards are only a cheap pre-filter. Every `workflow_run`
  consumer first runs the same inline **Verify trusted trigger** step. It reads
  the event file, never interpolation, and fails the job unless all of these hold:
  - the producer `path` and `workflow_id` match a `TRUSTED_PRODUCERS` line
    (`<file> <workflow ID> <exact branch> <events> <conclusions>`);
  - branch, event, conclusion and head repository name and ID match exactly;
  - the head SHA is reachable from the branch: compare status `behind` or
    `identical` against `refs/heads/<branch>`. The base is fully qualified
    because GitHub resolves a bare name to a same-named tag first, and a tag
    push reports the tag name as `head_branch`. Tag pushes also ignore `paths`
    filters. The Discord Modal deploy sets `REQUIRE_BRANCH_TIP` and accepts
    only `identical`, the live branch tip. It also sets
    `TIP_TREE_PATH: apps/discord`. Its CI runs only for
    Discord changes, so unrelated commits often land on `main` while it runs.
    A `behind` head is therefore accepted only when the `apps/discord` tree at
    that head equals the tree at the tip of `refs/heads/main`, read with
    `git/ref` and contents GETs. The gate runs again as the first step of every
    job that checks out code. Re-running an old run, or only its failed deploy
    job, is therefore rejected once the deployed code has changed on the
    branch. Supabase Staging deliberately accepts any SHA reachable from
    `refs/heads/main`. Production sync may promote a `main` SHA that is no
    longer the tip, and that SHA's production migration needs its staging
    marker, which binds the trust step's verified SHA, never the raw event.
    An older SHA can run after a descendant already applied newer
    migrations, and `db push` refuses migration versions that exist only on
    the remote. The deploy step therefore compares versions first:
    - a staging version that is not on `main` fails closed (no push, no
      marker);
    - if every local version is applied and staging is ahead only with
      `main`'s versions, it skips the push and records the marker with an
      "already applied by a descendant" notice;
    - otherwise it pushes as before, including when the remote listing cannot
      be read.

    `scripts/ci/staging-descendant-marker.test.js` covers these cases;
  - manual runs start from exactly `TRUSTED_DISPATCH_REF`.

  Checkouts use the step's verified `head_sha`, and secret-bearing steps and jobs
  are gated on its `trusted` output. Workflow IDs are stable per file path. If a
  producer file is renamed or recreated, update its line (`gh api
  repos/<repo>/actions/workflows/<file> --jq .id`); until then the gate fails
  closed. `scripts/ci/workflow-run-trigger-gate.test.js` runs the real step against
  case variants, tag sources, spoofed producers and head-repository mismatches.
- A pinned production sync must use a SHA whose Supabase Staging Migration
  succeeded. Otherwise the production migration finds no staging marker for
  that SHA and waits.
- Supabase Production accepts a staging migration marker only when the
  producer's `supabase-staging.yaml` blob is allowlisted. Keep the list to the
  current blob plus blobs from `main`'s history; drop blobs from rejected or
  intermediate branch heads. `scripts/ci/staging-contract-allowlist.test.js`
  pins the list exactly.
  The direct-push producer blob is eligible only for `push` with
  `run.head_sha == target`; older blobs retain their prior wrapper/dispatch rules.
  The new workflow's manual repairs are staging-only evidence and are excluded
  from production marker selection after their producer identity and immutable
  source are verified. A later manual marker cannot displace an earlier eligible
  push marker; selected evidence retains every run, attempt, status and job check.
  Add a changed producer blob and its event-protocol classification in the same PR, preserving
  every accepted historical blob and its admission rules.
  Run the full `node scripts/run-script-tests.js` collector, including
  `staging-contract-allowlist`, `production-migration-target` and
  `staging-descendant-marker`, plus the push trigger/consumer negatives.
- Ineligible runs (spoofed completions, dispatches from other refs) take a
  private `supabase-staging-migration-ignored-<run>` lock, so they never queue
  with real migrations. Case variants can pass GitHub's case-insensitive
  prefilter; the shell proof rejects them before checkout.
- The source binds staging credentials to `supabase-staging-migrations`. Keep its
  deployment branch policy restricted to `main` (not `supabase-staging`, which holds
  the deployment markers Supabase Production reads). Add a tag ruleset that blocks
  creating `main` and `production` tags; `head_branch` cannot tell a tag apart from
  a branch with the same name.
- The staging deploy step runs `supabase db push --include-all` after linking
  the staging Supabase project, so staging can converge after `main` migration
  history changes.
- This means `main` is where app preview and staging schema advancement are
  meant to stay aligned.
- For historical recovery, rerun an existing eligible producer for that exact
  target. A manual run of the new push workflow cannot unlock production. If no
  eligible producer exists, hold promotion for release-owner recovery; do not
  forge markers or bypass the production proof.
- Satellite production web deploys run through `vercel-production-<app>.yaml`.
- A production push first runs `vercel-production.yaml`, which computes affected
  Vercel and Cloudflare apps in one runner and calls only the necessary per-app
  workflows. Each target uses its own last successful deployment marker, so an
  app skipped on an earlier commit still receives any undeployed changes.
- Hosted `apps/web` production deploys run through
  `vercel-production-platform.yaml`; self-hosted machines still use the Docker
  release flow below for their own runtime deployment.
- `apps/apps` production deploys are handled by `vercel-production-apps.yaml`.
- `apps/qr` production deploys are handled by `vercel-production-qr.yaml`.
- Each production app uses a workflow-and-branch concurrency group whose
  `cancel-in-progress` predicate matches only `production` push events, so the
  newest production SHA remains deployable without letting `main` commits or
  manual recovery runs cancel it.
- Production deploy jobs are bound to `vercel-production-<app>` GitHub
  Environments and reject manual dispatches unless the selected branch is
  `production`.

### Hosted Calendar schedules

Infrastructure owns the hosted Calendar provider-sync (every 15 minutes) and
smart-scheduling (every six hours) schedules in its `vercel.json` and
`cron.config.json`. Requests enter `/api/cron/calendar/:job`, authenticate with
`CRON_SECRET`, and use the encrypted gateway credential to reach Calendar.
Calendar must not keep a second direct Vercel schedule: direct scheduler requests
do not carry the private hosting header.

The retired Docker configuration retains these jobs in
`apps/web/cron.config.json` with `vercel: false`. That flag excludes them from
generated Web Vercel schedules; it does not activate a Docker runner. The
Infrastructure hosted schedules are the active Calendar owners. After deployment, verify a fresh provider sync timestamp
with all Calendar clients closed; a READY deployment alone is insufficient.

### Browser App Version Metadata

- Browser apps share one platform version from
  `packages/utils/src/platform-release.ts`; do not read visible app versions
  from individual app `package.json` files.
- The shared browser app version is the `TUTURUUU_PLATFORM_VERSION` constant
  exported from `packages/utils/src/platform-release.ts`. Release Please owns
  that value (it carries the `x-release-please-version` annotation), so do not
  pin a literal version in docs or bump it by hand. Read the constant directly
  when you need the current value.
- Every Vercel browser app workflow runs
  `bun run --silent scripts/ci/generate-build-metadata.ts` before
  `vercel build`. The generated metadata includes the commit hash, short hash,
  commit message, ref, environment, deployment URL, deployment stamp, and build
  timestamp.
- The account-scoped version badge uses `public.user_configs` key
  `SHOW_VERSION_BADGE`. It is hidden by default and only exact
  `@tuturuuu.com` accounts may enable a truthy value.
- Exact-domain enforcement happens on the server through
  `isExactTuturuuuDotComEmail`; subdomains such as `@xwf.tuturuuu.com` are not
  eligible, and client cookies cannot make the badge render for ineligible
  users.

### Production Database

`supabase-production.yaml` is stricter than staging:

1. It re-evaluates automatically after either `Vercel Production Deployment
   Planner` completes its selected production deploys on `production` or
   `Supabase Staging Migration` completes on `main`.
2. The production planner for the target commit must have concluded
   successfully on `production`, and the selected platform deployment must have
   recorded the successful
   `vercel-production-platform` deployment marker for the same SHA. A workflow
   run that skipped because package releases were still publishing is not
   enough.
3. The `main` staging migration for the same target commit must have completed
   with a `success` conclusion.
4. A manual dispatch can still be used when an operator explicitly wants to run
   it, but the dispatch must select the `production` branch and still satisfy
   the same production-deployment and staging-migration SHA checks.

The staging-triggered path is an automatic retry for the case where production
production deploy finishes before staging migration does. The production
migration job still checks out the verified target commit explicitly before
running `supabase db push --include-all`. This keeps production schema changes
behind application deployment, staging validation, and branch promotion
for the same commit.

## Self-Hosted Web Release Flow

If a server receives code through `git pull`, use the Docker production commands from
the checked-out commit:

- `bun serve:web:docker` for in-place replacement
- `bun serve:web:docker:bg` for blue/green rebuild-before-cutover deployment

Blue/green is the safer path when uptime matters because the new image is built and
health-checked before the proxy is reloaded.

## Inactive migration and retained Docker tooling

`apps/tanstack-web` and `apps/backend` are not in use. Their source and runbooks
are retained for a possible future resumption; they are not release dependencies
for the live Next.js apps. Migration-specific builds, workers, Docker comparisons,
and cutover gates must not be required for ordinary Next.js delivery. Keep source
tracking required by repository policy without claiming a runtime cutover.

Docker setup is also outside the current supported path, and the Docker cron
runner is retired. The earlier self-hosted commands in this page are retained
reference procedures. Hosted Vercel/Cloudflare delivery and the owning scheduler
configuration establish active release behavior. See the
[active runtime map](/build/devops/active-runtime).

## Team Release Checklist

1. Merge the change set with green CI.
2. Docker setup is inactive; do not require or run `docker-setup-check.yaml` until explicitly resumed.
3. If database migrations changed, confirm the `main`-driven staging path first.
   Check that app code remains usable against the old production schema: the
   production Vercel planner deploys apps before the production migration job
   runs, and the job may wait in the Actions queue.
4. Promote to `production` only after preview and staging behavior is understood.
5. Confirm that the follow-up Supabase workflow's **Migrate production database**
   job actually ran and applied the expected migration. A successful prerequisite
   job can leave the migration job skipped.
6. For schema-dependent app releases, test the new deployment's authenticated
   read path against production after the migration and confirm the public alias
   points to that tested deployment.
7. For self-hosted rollout, deploy from the intended commit and prefer `bun serve:web:docker:bg`.

## Rollback Guidance

- Vercel-hosted rollback: for satellite apps, redeploy the previous known-good commit or use Vercel rollback tooling.
- If an app reads a production column that has not migrated yet, roll back only
  that app to a tested deployment. Keep the migration workflow running, then
  test the newer deployment directly against the migrated database before
  promoting its alias again. Verify the public URL after both changes.
- Supabase rollback: use a corrective migration instead of editing applied migration history.
- Self-hosted Docker rollback: checkout the previous known-good commit and rerun `bun serve:web:docker:bg`.

## What Not To Do

- Do not push production schema changes directly from a laptop as the normal path.
- Do not assume staging and production migrations are interchangeable; they are gated differently.
- Do not manually dispatch production Supabase migration from `main`; the only
  valid `main` path is the automatic staging-migration re-evaluation, and the
  production gate still requires the same commit to have both a successful
  production platform deployment and a completed successful `main` staging
  migration.
- Do not use the in-place Docker path when you specifically need rebuild-before-restart semantics.

## Migrated Supabase CI baseline

E2E jobs share a pristine database-volume snapshot, in addition to the existing
Supabase service image cache. The exact fingerprint includes migration contents,
seed files, local configuration, setup code, CLI/service versions, and runner
architecture. A UTC-day seed epoch bounds time-relative fixture staleness and stays
fixed throughout a job. There are no partial restore keys. Only trusted `main` runs publish
a snapshot, before tests create users or other mutable fixtures.

The setup action refuses an existing database volume. It verifies archive integrity,
the Postgres image digest, and migration history before using a restored database;
a mismatch or corrupt snapshot rebuilds from migrations. Snapshots are copied only
after PostgreSQL stops cleanly. Each job gets its own volume. Gateway model metadata
is refreshed after restoring, so it is not frozen into the baseline. Production and
staging database deployments do not use these local test snapshots.

Keep an uncached migration run in validation when changing migrations or the cache
format. Compare cold and warm setup times before claiming a performance gain. The
helper refuses execution outside a fresh Linux GitHub Actions runner and must never
be used to archive a developer or production database.

The Supabase baseline fingerprint includes the configured image registry as well
as the image version. CI uses `public.ecr.aws` without a registry login and honors
`SUPABASE_INTERNAL_IMAGE_REGISTRY` for restore
integrity checks. Its contract also transfers the pristine snapshot to a separate
runner and requires a verified restore, so a safe cold fallback cannot hide a
broken cross-runner cache. Restore failures report only their phase, without
printing credential-bearing child-process output.
